newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Dec 13.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Noranda Inc and Comalco Ltd said on Thursday that Comalco was withdrawing from its option to buy into Noranda's Alumysa aluminum project in southern Chile. Comalco said its first priorities were completing a major expansion at the Boyne Island smelter in Queensland, Australia and an upgrade at the Tiwai Point aluminum smelter in New Zealand, the companies said.

ICI Australia Ltd is considering building a A$2 billion petrochemicals plant in Western Australia to use natural gas from the North West Shelf project, the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Friday. Chief executive Warren Haynes was quoted as saying the project, if it proceeded, would probably be done in partnership. "It's a huge project. It will be export oriented. A world-scale plant would cost A$2 billion," he was quoted as saying.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$17.48 (-0.07)

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Thursday that the current president and chief executive of BHP Copper, Burgess Winter, would retire from January 1, and be replaced by Jim Lewis, who is currently BHP's executive general management of corporate development. Newspapers said Winter's resignation was after less than a year in the position.

Qantas Airways Ltd said on Thursday that it would negotiate with start-up airline Aussie Airlines Pty Ltd with a view to entering into sub-leases at some of its terminals. The proposed negotiations follow a settlement between Qantas and the Federal Airports Corp (FAC) after the FAC threatened to sue Qantas for allegedly breaching the terms of its leases by refusing to offer terminal space to Aussie Airlines.

Drug developer Cortecs International Ltd said on Thursday it had signed an agreement with Cancer Research Campaign Technology Ltd (CRCT) for the development of diagnostic tests for nasopharngeal cancer.
